operations.summary: Returns the OIDC discovery document so clients learn endpoints, supported algorithms (`EdDSA` for tokens, `ES256` for DPoP) and the PKCE method `S256`. Cacheable for 1 h.
Returns the public signing keys for access and ID tokens; during rotation two keys are listed (SEC-CR). Cacheable for 10 min.

Starts an authorization-code flow with PKCE and redirects the system browser to the hosted sign-in UI; only registered exact `redirect_uri` values are accepted, and errors never redirect to an unregistered URI (no open redirect).

Exchanges an authorization code (with `code_verifier`), a refresh token (rotation, SEC-AU-5), client credentials (`cp-ssr`) or the anonymous grant (SEC-AU-14) for tokens; mobile requests carry a DPoP proof with a server nonce, BFFs authenticate with `private_key_jwt` over mTLS.
operations.sec: PUB(no token) ATT(anonymous grant, cp-mobile code grant) RL(auth.signin)

operations.summary: Revokes a refresh token (and its family) or an access token's session; always returns 200 so token validity cannot be probed.
Issues a proof-of-work challenge for clients that cannot attest (SEC-BF-7); the difficulty grows with the risk score of the IP prefix and device.

Creates an account inside the current sign-in interaction (email + password, or email/phone for OTP-only sign-up) and sends a verification; the response is identical whether or not the email already exists (SEC-AU-11).
operations.inputType: { interaction_id: Id; full_name: Str<2,100>; email: Email; password?: Str<12,128>; phone?: Phone; locale: Locale; terms_version: Str<1,20>; privacy_policy_version: Str<1,20> }

operations.summary: Verifies email and password inside the interaction and returns the next step (MFA or complete); every failure is `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` with a fixed minimum latency.
operations.inputType: { interaction_id: Id; email: Email; password: Str<1,128> }

operations.summary: Sends a one-time sign-in or verification code to an email or a phone number on the region allowlist; always `202` with the same body.
operations.inputType: { interaction_id: Id; channel: 'email'|'sms'; destination: Email | Phone; purpose: 'signin'|'verify' }

operations.summary: Checks the one-time code; five wrong codes invalidate it (SEC-AU-8).
Returns WebAuthn request or creation options (challenge valid 5 min, `userVerification: required`, RP ID `carpal.app`) for sign-in, second factor or step-up.
Completes the second factor with a TOTP code, a WebAuthn assertion or a recovery code, and raises the interaction to `aal2` (or `aal3` for hardware WebAuthn).
operations.inputType: { interaction_id: Id; method: 'totp_mfa'|'webauthn'|'recovery_code'; code?: Code6; recovery_code?: Str<10,20>; assertion?: Json<WebAuthnAssertion> }

operations.summary: Starts Google or Apple sign-in inside the interaction; linking to an existing account follows SEC-AU-13.
Consumes an `ev` link token and marks the email verified; the account becomes `active` when its first contact is verified.
Sends a password-reset link if the email belongs to an account; the response never reveals whether it does.
Consumes a `pr` token, sets the new password and revokes every session and refresh token of the account.
Returns the caller's account, preferences, memberships (for the role and organization switcher) and plan summary.
Updates the caller's own name, display name, locale, timezone and preferred contact channel.
Starts an email change: a verification link goes to the new address and a notice to the old one; the change applies only after verification.
Sends a code to a new phone number on the region allowlist.
Confirms the new phone number with the code and replaces the old one.
Changes the password after checking the current one and revokes all other sessions.
Returns the caller's display, privacy, notification-mode and AI preferences.
Updates preferences; enabling AI personalization or marketing needs the matching active consent, and `navigation_app_key` must be in the region list.
Lists the caller's role memberships, including the implicit `individual` role, for the role and organization switcher.
Leaves an organization; the last active owner of an organization cannot leave.
Lists the caller's active sessions and devices.
Signs out one session (use the current session ID to sign out).
Signs out every session except, optionally, the current one, and revokes all refresh tokens.
Lists the caller's second-factor methods.
Creates a pending TOTP method and returns its provisioning URI once; it becomes active after `me.mfa_confirm`.
Returns WebAuthn creation options for registering a passkey or security key.
Activates a pending TOTP method with a code, or a WebAuthn credential with its attestation, and returns 10 recovery codes once if this is the first method.
Removes a second-factor method; staff accounts cannot remove their last WebAuthn credential.
Replaces all recovery codes and returns the new set once.
Lists the caller's consent records, active and withdrawn.
Records a new consent, optionally scoped to one record and granted to one party; records are immutable except withdrawal.
Withdraws a consent with immediate effect on all dependent sharing (SEC-AZ-8).
Shows what a business is asking consent for (for example a showcase of the caller's car) from a `cn` link, without consuming it.
Grants or declines a consent request from a `cn` link; a grant creates the scoped `ConsentRecord`.
Lists an organization's consents (AI use of fleet data, provider analytics or private inventory).
Records an organization-level consent; only the organization owner can give it.
operations.inputNote: consent_type limited to the three organization types above

operations.summary: Withdraws an organization-level consent immediately; dependent AI features stop for that organization.
Files an export, deletion, rectification or consent-withdrawal request; identity is re-verified by step-up, and the deadline comes from policy.
Lists the caller's data subject requests.
Returns one data subject request.
Returns a 5-minute signed download URL for a completed export (SEC-UP-4).
Returns the caller's onboarding progress for every flow.
Saves the current step of one flow; steps are keys from the WP0 journey maps.
Records the owner's acceptance of the business terms after staff-assisted onboarding; staff cannot do this for the owner.
Creates a provider, vendor, fleet or hybrid organization; the caller becomes its owner and the organization gets the default plan of its audience. A verified contact is required.
Returns the organization as seen by a member, including the caller's role.
Updates the organization's names, contacts, description and slug.
Lists members and pending invitations of the organization (team users, fleet staff and drivers).
Sends a single-use `mi` invitation link to an email address for a role that is not higher than the inviter's role.
operations.sec: ORG(M+, FC: fleet_driver only) IDEM RL(default.write) AUD

operations.summary: Accepts an organization invitation; the signed-in user's verified email must match the invited email (SEC-LT-5).
Changes a member's role or suspends/reactivates them; only the owner can grant owner or manager roles.
Removes a member or revokes an invitation; their sessions lose this organization context immediately (SEC-AU-3).
operations.sec: ORG(O+, M+: lower roles only) AUD

operations.summary: Lists the organization's locations with exact coordinates.

Adds a location with its exact point (shops and sellers must give their exact location: a map pin, or a map link resolved with `geo.resolve_map_link`); the server geocodes the address, computes the pin-versus-address check and the public point. A `far_apart` result warns but does not block.
Updates a location; moving the pin or changing the address re-runs the check and clears `location_verified_at`.
Deactivates a location; the primary location cannot be removed while it is the only active one.
Checks a pin against a typed address before saving, using the self-hosted geocoder of the region.
operations.inputType: { address_line_1: Str<2,160>; city: Str<1,100>; postal_code?: Str<1,20>; country: Country; pin: GeoPoint }

operations.summary: Searches addresses in the launch region for the business location editor; it is not offered to consumers as search-as-you-type (Plan §2).
Returns the nearest address for a pin in the business location editor.

Turns a shared map link (for example a Google Maps URL, or a regional map app link from the region allowlist) into an exact point that the owner then confirms on the map; full URLs with coordinates are parsed without any network call, and short links are expanded only under SEC-IN-9. The point is never saved automatically.
operations.responseType: { point: GeoPoint; provider_key: Str<1,40>; label: Str<1,300> | null }

operations.summary: Lists the organization's verification checks and their outcomes.
Submits a verification check with private documents for admin review (MVP §13).
Returns the provider profile with completeness and the criteria still missing.
Creates or replaces the provider profile fields; system fields (completeness, measured response time, activity) are computed.
Publishes the provider profile when the publish rules hold (active organization, active location, service category, supported brand; 52 §21); otherwise lists what is missing.
Takes the profile off public search, the map and profile pages; existing appointments continue.
Lists certifications with their verification status.
Adds a certification; with a clean private document it enters the admin verification queue, and only verified certifications count as evidence.
Updates a certification; changing the document or credential resets verification to `pending`.
Removes a certification; linked capability evidence is revoked.
Lists the service catalog, including AI-suggested rows waiting for approval.
Adds a service system or task to the catalog (unique per node), with source `self_declared`.
Updates a catalog entry's display text, level, price indicator, duration, appointment types or visibility.
Deactivates a catalog entry.
Lists supported brands, models, series, engines and fuel types.
Adds up to 200 coverage rows in one request (unlimited in total, MVP Module C); each row is validated independently and duplicates are skipped.
operations.responseType: { created: List<Coverage,200>; skipped: List<{ index: Int<0,199>; code: FieldErrorCode }, 200> }

operations.summary: Deactivates one coverage row.
Lists the capability matrix with computed confidence and evidence counts.
Declares a capability (`self_declared`, confidence level 0); confidence grows only from evidence, and self-declared claims never earn badges.
Changes the declared experience level or public visibility; a capability becomes public only when approved and at least `low_evidence`.
Deactivates a capability; its evidence links stay for audit.
Lists the evidence behind one capability with weights and dates.

Approves or rejects a record that AI suggested (catalog entry, coverage row, capability or AI-linked evidence); nothing AI-suggested becomes public or counted without this decision ("AI suggests, provider approves, platform verifies").
Lists logged jobs.
Logs a completed job as evidence; a customer vehicle can be linked only with the customer's consent.
Corrects a job log; verification status is system-set.
Removes a job log and revokes its evidence.
Lists private notes about one customer; notes are visible only to provider members and are included in the customer's data export.
Adds a private note about a customer who has an appointment or service record with this provider.
Edits a note.
Removes a note.
Lists portfolio items in any status.
Creates a portfolio item in `draft`; media are attached with `media.attach` (roles `before`/`after` paired by `pair_group_key`).
Edits a draft or published item; editing a published item returns it to `pending_review`.
Asks the customer of a linked appointment or service record for showcase consent by a `cn` link; the server derives the customer from the visit, so a provider cannot target arbitrary users.
Submits an item for publication; it is published only with at least one approved media, required customer consent and moderation approval.
Archives an item and removes it from public pages and search.
Returns the provider dashboard figures: completeness, response time, ratings by category, profile and map views, directions taps and request sources.
Returns the vendor profile with quality and completeness scores.
Creates or replaces the vendor profile fields.
Publishes the vendor profile and its public inventory when the publish rules hold (active organization, active location, profile complete enough, an active item or "catalog coming soon").
Removes the vendor and its items from public search and the map.
Lists supported brands, models and part categories.
Adds up to 200 coverage rows; duplicates are skipped.
operations.responseType: { created: List<VendorCoverage,200>; skipped: List<{ index: Int<0,199>; code: FieldErrorCode }, 200> }

operations.summary: Deactivates a coverage row.
Returns vendor analytics: inquiries, fulfilment, response time, catalog quality, missing fitment and images, searched and popular categories, map views and directions taps.
Lists the active plans and their entitlements for plan pages and upgrade prompts. Cacheable for 10 min.
Returns the caller's personal subscription (always at least Individual Free), effective entitlements and usage, for the plan and vehicle-limit screen.
Returns the organization's subscription, effective entitlements and usage.
Asks CarPal to change the organization's plan; in the MVP plans are assigned manually by an admin (`admin.subscription_assign`), so this only records the request and notifies staff.
Returns the current taxonomy version so clients can refresh cached snapshots only when it changes. Cacheable for 5 min.
Returns all active nodes of one type (optionally under one parent) in the requested locale for client-side pickers; versioned by `ETag` and cacheable for 1 h.
Returns one node, including merged nodes so stale references can be followed to `merged_into_id`.
Typeahead over node names and synonyms in any enabled language, with character, digit and transliteration normalization (Persian typed in Latin letters matches).
operations.inputType: { text: Str<1,100>; types: Set<TaxonomyType,5>; parent_id?: Id }

operations.summary: Lists the caller's vehicles (personal) or the fleet's vehicles; a fleet driver sees only assigned vehicles.
Adds a vehicle by VIN or manual entry; active vehicles cannot exceed the plan's `max_vehicles` (Individual Free 5), checked in the same transaction.
Returns one vehicle.
Updates any vehicle field (manual override always allowed, even after VIN decoding); a new VIN re-runs duplicate detection.
Changes the vehicle status (active, inactive, sold, in repair, archived) and writes status history; returning a vehicle to `active` or `in_repair` counts toward the vehicle limit.
Returns the full decrypted VIN to the owner or a fleet manager after step-up; every reveal is audited.
operations.sec: USR | ORG(F+) AAL2 AUD PII RL(default.write)

operations.summary: "Did you buy this car?" (GD-33): asks the current owner of a VIN that is registered to someone else to transfer the vehicle to the caller. The owner is notified and never disclosed; on acceptance the vehicle and every record linked to it move to the caller. Requests expire after 14 days.

errors.detail: the caller already owns it or asked already

operations.summary: Lists transfer requests the caller made (outgoing) or received as current owner (incoming).

The current owner accepts or rejects a pending request; acceptance moves the vehicle with its service records, documents, issues, reminders, mileage and media to the buyer and clears the previous owner's nickname, plate and notes.
The buyer withdraws a pending request.
Runs the optional VIN decoder and returns suggested field values without applying them; the owner applies them with `vehicles.update`.
Lists the vehicle's status changes (used for fleet downtime).
Lists mileage readings.
Records a mileage reading and updates the vehicle's current mileage; a lower reading is accepted with a warning flag.
Lists the vehicle's documents (insurance, registration, warranty, invoices, inspection reports).
Stores a document as private encrypted media; sharing with a provider needs an active `vehicle_data_sharing` consent scoped to that provider.
operations.sec: USR | ORG(FC) IDEM CNS(vehicle_data_sharing: if shared_with_provider)

operations.summary: Changes a document's title, dates or visibility.
operations.sec: USR | ORG(FC) ETAG CNS(vehicle_data_sharing: if shared_with_provider)

operations.summary: Removes a document; its media follows the retention policy.
Returns the vehicle's service history timeline, newest first, with verified and self-reported records clearly marked.
Adds a manual or invoice-based service record; an invoice upload starts the invoice verification path.
Returns one service record with its evidence.
Edits a record the caller created; provider-created and appointment records can only be disputed (`disputes.create`).
Removes a record the caller created; records used as review or capability evidence are kept for audit and hidden.
Attaches an invoice, photo or document to a record.
Removes a piece of evidence.

Lets a provider enter a service record for a customer's vehicle ("basic service history entry for customers"), either through an appointment or with the customer's vehicle-sharing consent; it is `provider_logged` and `provider_confirmed`.
Lists active and resolved issues of a vehicle.
Reports an issue; the server runs the shared safety keyword check, and a fleet driver's report starts the fleet approval workflow (`fleet_approval_status = pending`).
Returns one issue with its triage and approval links.
Edits the issue text, symptom or urgency; urgency cannot be set below the level the safety check set.
Moves an issue to investigating, resolved or cancelled (scheduled is set by appointments).
Lists maintenance reminders of a vehicle.
Adds a manual reminder due by date, mileage or both.
Snoozes, completes or dismisses a reminder, or edits a manual one.
Deletes a manual reminder.
Lists the vendor's own items with structured filters (no free text in the URL; text search is `inventory.search`).
Searches the vendor's own items by SKU, part number or name.
operations.inputType: { text: Str<1,100>; cursor?: Cursor; limit?: Int<1,50> }

operations.summary: Creates an item; active items are limited by `max_inventory_items`, and the SKU is unique within the vendor.
Returns one item including trade price and internal notes.
Updates an item; price and visibility changes reach the public projection through `inventory.updated`.
Marks an item `removed`; it leaves public search at once.
Changes stock status, visibility, status or price-on-request for up to 500 items in one background job.
Confirms that an item duplicates another of the vendor's items, or clears the mark.
Lists fitment rows of an item, including AI suggestions waiting for confirmation.
Adds up to 100 fitment rows (`source = manual`); `confirmed` requires the vendor's own confirmation, which this operation records.
operations.responseType: { created: List<Fitment,100>; skipped: List<{ index: Int<0,99>; code: FieldErrorCode }, 100> }

operations.summary: Edits a fitment row.
Deactivates a fitment row.
Confirms or rejects an AI-suggested fitment row; only confirmation sets `confirmed` (52 InventoryFitment).
Starts a CSV import in the background with the given column mapping (≤ 20,000 rows, SEC-IN-11); the UI is not blocked.
Lists import batches.
Returns one import batch with its counts.
Returns a 5-minute signed URL for the CSV of row errors (formula-safe, SEC-IN-11).
Lists trade relationship requests and approved trade customers.
Approves, rejects or revokes a trade account; only approved trade customers see trade-only items and trade prices.
Lists the vendor's stock inquiries grouped as open, answered, reserved or closed.
Returns one inquiry with its message thread.
Replies to an inquiry; the first reply moves it from `sent` to `answered` and sets `first_response_at`.
Moves an inquiry to reserved, unavailable, answered or completed by the vendor side rules.
Sends a stock inquiry about an item visible to the caller; a vehicle context is shared only through the atomic `vendor_fitment_context` consent, and the snapshot never contains VIN or plate.
Lists the requester's inquiries.
Returns one inquiry with its messages.
Adds a message to the thread.
Cancels an inquiry or marks it completed ("I picked it up"); a completed inquiry lets the requester review the vendor on Path 1.
Asks a vendor for a trade account on behalf of a provider or fleet organization.
Lists the organization's trade accounts with vendors.

Runs one search (direct search, map list, Help Me follow-up or fleet search): normalizes the text, interprets it into editable chips, runs the server-side safety check, ranks results with stored structured reasons and returns the first page. Plan, payment or sponsorship never affects ranking.
Returns the next page of a search session owned by the caller.
Re-runs a session with edited chips, filters, location or vehicle filter and returns a new session; the ranking rules are unchanged.
operations.inputType: { intent_override?: InterpretedIntent; filters?: SearchFilters; location?: LocationInput; vehicle_filter_applied?: boolean; sort?: 'best_match'|'distance'|'rating' }

operations.summary: Records that a result was viewed or selected (match acceptance metric).
Returns one pin per business location in the viewport (public fields only, public points, clusters by zoom), with highlight and vehicle-relevance flags; never any featured or paid pin.

emits.note: analytics, first call of a map session

operations.summary: Runs the shared safety keyword check on free text (request descriptions, issue text) so clients can show the safety banner before sending; the same check runs again on submission.
Returns the public profile of a published provider, vendor or hybrid by slug (SEO pages), with only approved, evidence-backed capabilities, verified certifications and active badges.
Lists published reviews of an organization; both confirmation paths are shown with their labels, and there is no "unverified" section.
Lists published portfolio items (before/after showcases) of a provider.

Searches a vendor's public items; at least one of text, category or vehicle is required (SEC-BF-4), trade-only items and trade prices appear only for members of an organization with an approved trade account.
operations.inputType: { text?: Str<1,100>; part_category_node_id?: Id; vehicle_id?: Id; vehicle?: { brand_node_id: Id; model_node_id?: Id; series_node_id?: Id; year?: Int<1950,2100> }; as_organization_id?: Id; cursor?: Cursor; limit?: Int<1,50> }

operations.summary: Returns one public or permitted trade-only item with its fitment and vendor card.
Returns open appointment slots of a provider location for up to 14 days, computed from availability rules, buffers, capacity and time off.

Tells the caller whether they can review an organization and which path applies, listing their eligible visits (confirmed appointments, completed inquiries, verified service records) and whether each is inside the 7-day window.

Submits a review; the server chooses Path 1 (visit evidence, published after automatic checks, no business approval) or Path 2 (`pending_approval`, needs the business's confirmation or the 7-day no-objection rule plus a CarPal reviewer). An `invitation_grant` consumes its single-use invitation atomically.
Lists the caller's reviews in every status ("Waiting for approval" shows here).
Returns one of the caller's reviews with its status and path.
Edits a review before it is published; the edit restarts the automatic checks. A rating change never affects the approval decision.
Withdraws the caller's review (status `removed`, kept for audit and hidden).
Adds evidence media (invoice, photo) to a Path 2 review or an objection dispute (`MediaAttachment` role `evidence`, visible only to CarPal staff).
Lists the caller's open in-app review invitations.

Opens an invitation link: records `opened_at`, sends the one-time code to the invited contact and returns the visit context; an expired or used link returns `410` with a way to review from the profile (Path 2).
Checks the one-time code for a signed-in invitee and returns a 30-minute grant bound to the user and the invitation for `reviews.create`.
operations.responseType: { invitation_grant: Str<20,200>; expires_at: DateTime; path: ConfirmationPath }

operations.summary: Sends a review invitation for one visit to its customer by in-app notification or email (email needs the customer's `review_invitations` consent); invitations for provider job logs count as the business's confirmation, and self-review patterns are blocked.
operations.sec: ORG(P*, V*) IDEM RL(review.invite) CNS(review_invitations: email) FLAG(reviews.invitation_email.enabled: email)

operations.summary: Lists the organization's invitations with conversion status.
Cancels a pending or sent invitation; its link stops working.
Lists reviews about the organization (review inbox), without internal AI flags.
Returns one review about the organization with its response draft.
Creates a response draft, optionally from an AI draft insight; AI drafts are never published without this human flow.
Edits a response draft or a published response (re-moderated).
Publishes the response; at most one published response per review.
Removes a response (draft or published).
Lists Path 2 reviews waiting for the business's answer ("Do you recognise this customer?"), showing only the visit context and the author's display name.

Answers the relationship question; `confirmed` passes the review to the CarPal reviewer, `rejected` never removes it but opens a `review_approval_objection` dispute decided by CarPal. No answer within 7 days counts as no objection.
operations.inputNote: note is visible to CarPal staff only

operations.summary: Opens a dispute or mediation request about a review, service record, badge, appointment or moderation action; outcomes feed trust signals.
Lists disputes raised by the caller or by organizations where the caller is a manager or owner.
Returns one dispute the caller raised or is party to.
Withdraws an open dispute raised by the caller.
Lists the provider's badges with rule key, version and the evaluation snapshot (auditable, rule-based).
Lists the organization's own trust signals and score components (risk and authenticity signals excluded).

Creates an appointment draft or request for a vehicle the caller owns or manages; the server runs the safety check on the description, enforces open-request caps and, for fleets with the workflow on, requires an approved approval. The appointment process has no review step and carries no review content: users check a shop's profile and reviews beforehand by tapping its name on a result card, map pin or the request draft (`public.org_get`, `public.org_reviews`).
Lists the requester's appointments grouped as upcoming, past, requested or cancelled.
Returns one appointment; the exact provider address appears once it is confirmed.
Edits a draft or a request that the provider has not started reviewing.
Applies a requester-side status change (submit, accept or counter an alternative, cancel).
Notifies the provider of a late arrival.
Checks the signed-in requester in, from 2 hours before to 2 hours after the confirmed start.
Checks in from a `ci` link without signing in (low-risk action, same time window).
Lists the status changes of an appointment.
Lists customer-visible notes (requester side never sees internal notes).
Adds a customer-visible note from the requester side.

Returns the pre-visit report as it will be shown to the provider, read-only ("See what the shop will receive"); for a draft it is the preview, including the AI summary when triage exists. There is no separate approval step: submitting the request (`submit = true` or draft → `requested`) is the user's approval of what the preview showed (SEC-AI-3).
Lists incoming and scheduled appointments of the provider.
Returns one appointment with the requester's contact from confirmation onward.
Sets duration, estimated completion window, parts note, location or cost estimate; a fleet estimate above the threshold creates a cost approval.
Applies a provider-side status change; confirmation re-checks capacity in the same transaction, and completion creates the service record and the review invitation.
Lists the people assigned to an appointment.
Assigns a staff member as service advisor or technician.
Removes an assigned staff member.
Lists internal and customer-visible notes.
Adds an internal or customer-visible note.

Returns the pre-visit report; history fields are filled only while the requester's `service_history_sharing` consent for this appointment is active, and "Triage: not provided" shows when there was no Help Me.
Returns the daily or weekly calendar: appointments, time off and used versus maximum capacity per slot.
Lists working-hour and slot rules.
Adds a weekly rule (hours, slot length, appointment types, concurrency, buffer) for a location.
operations.sec: ORG(P+) IDEM ENT(appointment_capacity_tools_enabled: concurrency > 1 or buffers)

operations.summary: Edits a rule; confirmed appointments are not changed.
Deactivates a rule.
Lists unavailable periods.
Blocks a period for one location or all locations; overlapping confirmed appointments are listed for the provider to handle.
Cancels a time-off period.
Declares an upload and returns a 10-minute pre-signed `PUT` for exactly that size, type and checksum (SEC-UP-1).
Uploads the bytes directly to object storage with the exact headers of the ticket; this is the only non-JSON request of the contract.
Finalizes the upload: verifies size and checksum, starts the malware scan, type detection, re-encoding and EXIF stripping; the asset is not servable until `scan_status = clean`.
Returns an asset the caller owns or can see, with its processing status.
Returns a short-lived signed URL (public 1 h, private 5 min) to the processed file for a viewer allowed by privacy level, consent and attachment rules.
Attaches an asset to an entity the caller may modify, with a role and an optional before/after pair key.
Changes order, caption, role or pair key of an attachment.
operations.inputType: { role?: AttachmentRole; pair_group_key?: Str<1,60> | null; display_order?: Int<0,1000>; caption?: Str<1,300> | null }

operations.summary: Removes an attachment; the asset remains for its other uses.
Removes an asset and all its attachments; deletion follows the retention policy.
Applies AI-suggested or hand-drawn redaction of plates and faces, or records that none is needed; a new processed variant replaces the display file.
Returns the fleet profile and approval settings.
Creates or updates the fleet profile; enabling the approval workflow needs the `fleet_approval_workflow_enabled` entitlement.
operations.sec: ORG(F+) ETAG(if exists) IDEM(if new) ENT(fleet_approval_workflow_enabled: if enabling) AUD

operations.summary: Returns fleet totals: vehicles, due for service, active repairs, open issues, pending approvals, monthly spend, most repaired vehicles, driver reports.
Lists driver assignments (one active per vehicle).
Assigns a driver to a vehicle and ends any previous active assignment in the same transaction.
Ends the vehicle's active assignment.
Lists preferred providers and approved vendors.
Adds a preferred provider or approved vendor, optionally for one service system or part category.
Changes priority, scope or notes, or deactivates a partner.
Lists approvals (repair request, provider selection, cost estimate).
Requests an approval, for example a coordinator proposing a provider for a driver's issue.
Returns one approval with its triage insight reference.
Approves, rejects or asks for more information; every decision is audited, and the requester cannot approve their own request.
Returns one fleet analytics report (cost by vehicle, month or category; repair and service frequency; downtime; provider usage; preferred provider performance; common issues).
Starts a CSV export in the background (formula-safe, SEC-IN-11).
operations.sec: ORG(F+, FR) IDEM ENT(export_enabled) ASYNC RL(export) AUD

operations.summary: Lists exports and their status.
Returns a 5-minute signed URL for a completed export.
Starts a CSV vehicle import; created vehicles still respect `max_vehicles`.
Lists vehicle import batches.
Returns a 5-minute signed URL for the row-error CSV.
Lists organizations the caller follows.
Follows a published provider or vendor (one active follow per pair) or changes its notification setting.
Unfollows an organization.
Lists saved favourite providers and vendors (an input to matching preferences).
Saves an organization as a favourite.
Removes a favourite.

Returns the focused Discover feed (nearby providers, relevant showcases, Q&A, maintenance tips, followed providers, recommendations for the caller's vehicles); computed, not stored, and never a full social feed.
operations.inputType: { location: LocationInput; vehicle_id?: Id; cursor?: Cursor; limit?: Int<1,50> }

operations.summary: Returns one published before/after showcase.
